name: Perseverance and Assurance

objectives.text: Identify Jesus as the Good Shepherd who knows His sheep, keeps them safe, and never loses them
Recall from Romans 8 that nothing in all creation can separate God's people from His love in Christ Jesus
Retell Philippians 1:6 in your own words to show that God finishes the good work He begins in His people
Explain from Scripture that believers are kept by God's power and Christ's prayer rather than by their own strength
Recite Heidelberg Catechism Q1 and explain how belonging to Christ in life and in death gives comfort to His people
Define the perseverance of the saints as the Reformed teaching that those God has effectually called can neither totally nor finally fall away from grace
Distinguish true believers from those who make only an outward profession of faith using the teaching of Jesus and John
Describe from the account of Peter's denial and restoration how a believer may fall into serious sin and yet be restored by Christ
Analyze how the Reformed tradition grounds perseverance in election, Christ's intercession, the indwelling Spirit, and the covenant of grace
Explain how God uses ordinary means such as the Word, the sacraments, and prayer to preserve believers in grace
Interpret the warning passages of Hebrews and 1 Corinthians in their context as means God uses to keep His people persevering
Identify the three grounds of assurance named by the Westminster Confession as God's promises, the inward evidences of grace, and the witness of the Spirit
Explain the Reformed distinction between perseverance as God's keeping and assurance as the believer's knowledge of it which may grow, be shaken, and be renewed
Analyze the tests of genuine faith in 1 John and explain how John intends them to give assurance rather than doubt
Evaluate the view that true believers can finally lose their salvation by weighing its arguments against Scripture and the Canons of Dort
Distinguish biblical assurance from presumption and careless security by explaining how the tradition holds that assurance moves believers toward holiness
Compare the Reformed teaching that ordinary believers may attain assurance with the Roman Catholic teaching that such certainty is not ordinarily possible
Construct a pastoral counsel from Scripture and the confessions for a believer who doubts their salvation

changes: Fixed the invalid reference by citing Jude as Jude 1:24-25. Kept the real competencies from the old list and reworded them as observable student tasks: Good Shepherd, Romans 8:38-39, Philippians 1:6, security resting in God, true versus outward profession, Heidelberg Q1 comfort, grounds of perseverance, warning passages, the ground of assurance, 1 John, the loss-of-salvation debate, and presumption. Folded covenant faithfulness into the grounds objective. Dropped the vague synthesis filler and the duplicate 'summarize perseverance' item, replacing it with a confessional definition. Added objectives on restoration after a fall (Peter), the ordinary means of preservation, the three grounds of assurance in WCF 18.2, assurance as distinct from perseverance and able to be shaken, the comparison with Roman Catholic teaching, and a culminating pastoral counsel for doubt. Updated confession citations to specific articles of WCF 17 and 18 and the Canons of Dort Head 5, and gave all scripture references verse ranges.
